docs.title: github-guard
docs.text:
Static security scanner for GitHub Actions workflows

Get Started GitHub

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
github-guard parses GitHub Actions workflow YAML files and composite actions, running 16 security checks across 6 categories. It catches trigger abuse, permission escalation, supply chain risks, secret hygiene issues, runner misconfigurations, and workflow flow vulnerabilities.

graph LR
    subgraph Input
        A[".github/workflows/*.yml"]
        B["action.yml"]
    end

    subgraph "github-guard"
        C[Parser] --> D[15 Security Checks]
        D --> E[FP Suppression]
    end

    subgraph Output
        F[JSON]
        G[SARIF 2.1.0]
        H[Text]
    end

    A --> C
    B --> C
    E --> F
    E --> G
    E --> H

Pipeline:

  1. Parser loads workflow YAML with ruamel.yaml, handles trigger normalization, composite actions, and reusable workflow calls
  2. 16 Security Checks across 6 categories detect trigger abuse, permission escalation, unpinned refs, secrets exposure, runner risks, and flow issues
  3. FP Suppression filters workflow_call-only workflows, trusted triggers, ${{ secrets.* }} references, and configurable safe lists

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
$ github-guard . --format text

GitHub Actions Security Scan: my-project
Found 4 issue(s)

[CRITICAL] GHA-TRIG-001: pull_request_target with fork checkout
  File: .github/workflows/ci.yml:15
  Job 'build' checks out fork code (ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }})
  in a pull_request_target workflow.
  Fix: Use pull_request trigger instead, or avoid checking out fork code.

[HIGH] GHA-PERM-001: Missing permissions block
  File: .github/workflows/ci.yml:1
  Workflow has no top-level permissions and not all jobs define permissions.
  Fix: Add a top-level 'permissions: {}' to restrict to read-only by default.

Summary: 1 CRITICAL, 1 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM

Generate SARIF for GitHub Code Scanning:

github-guard /path/to/repo --format sarif --output results.sarif

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Trigger Abuse Detection

    Detects pull_request_target + fork checkout (CRITICAL), bypassable fork detection gates, and workflow_dispatch command injection.

  • Supply Chain Pinning

    Flags unpinned action references (mutable tags like v4) and unpinned container images (:latest or missing tags). Validates composite actions.

  • Secret Hygiene

    Finds hardcoded credentials via pattern matching, secrets passed as workflow inputs instead of the secrets: key, and artifact uploads in PR target context.

  • Cross-Workflow Analysis

    Correlation checks detect workflow_run triggered by fork-triggerable workflows, tracing data flow risks across workflow boundaries.

docs.title: What Gets Detected
docs.text:
16 checks across 6 categories:

Category Checks Examples Triggers GHA-TRIG-001..004 pull_request_target + fork checkout, bypassable fork detection, workflow_dispatch injection, expression injection via attacker-controlled context Permissions GHA-PERM-001..002 Missing permissions block, id-token:write without OIDC consumer Pinning GHA-PIN-001..002 Unpinned action references, unpinned container images Secrets GHA-SEC-001..003 Hardcoded credentials, secrets as workflow inputs, artifact upload in PR context Runners GHA-RUN-001..002 Self-hosted runners without environment protection, jobs without timeout Flow GHA-FLOW-001..003 workflow_run from fork-triggerable source, composite action unpinned refs, secrets:inherit

See Detection Rules for the full reference.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: github-guard follows a pipeline architecture: parse, check, format.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
graph TD
    subgraph Input
        A["Repository path"] --> B["find_workflows()"]
        A --> C["find_composite_actions()"]
    end

    subgraph Parser
        B --> D["parse_workflow()"]
        C --> E["parse_composite_action()"]
        D --> F["GHAWorkflow"]
        E --> F
    end

    subgraph Checks
        F --> G["Per-workflow checks"]
        F --> H["Correlation checks"]
        G --> I["Findings"]
        H --> I
    end

    subgraph Output
        I --> J["FP suppression"]
        J --> K["Deduplication"]
        K --> L["format_json()"]
        K --> M["format_sarif()"]
        K --> N["format_text()"]
    end

docs.title: Parser (parser.py)
docs.text:
The parser uses ruamel.yaml (round-trip mode) to load workflow YAML while preserving line numbers. It produces a normalized data model:

  • GHAWorkflow: top-level workflow with name, triggers, permissions, env, and jobs
  • GHAJob: individual job with runs-on, permissions, environment, timeout, steps, and reusable workflow call info
  • GHAStep: individual step with uses, run, with, env, and if condition

Key behaviors:

  • normalize_triggers() handles all on: forms (string, list, dict)
  • Composite actions (action.yml) are modeled as single-job workflows with a composite_action trigger for uniform check processing
  • Both .github/workflows/*.yml and action.yml/action.yaml files are discovered

docs.title: Check Registry (checks/_common.py)
docs.text:
Checks register themselves via decorators:

  • @register_check: per-workflow checks that receive a single GHAWorkflow
  • @register_correlation_check: cross-workflow checks that receive all GHAWorkflow objects

Each check function returns a list of finding dicts. The _finding() helper ensures consistent structure with rule_id, severity, title, file, line, message, CWE, remediation, and docs_url.

docs.title: Check Modules
docs.text: Module Checks Focus triggers.py GHA-TRIG-001..003 Trigger abuse: PRT fork checkout, bypassable gates, dispatch injection permissions.py GHA-PERM-001..002 Permission escalation: missing permissions, OIDC token misuse pinning.py GHA-PIN-001..002 Supply chain: unpinned actions, unpinned container images secrets.py GHA-SEC-001..003 Secret hygiene: hardcoded creds, secrets as inputs, artifact upload runners.py GHA-RUN-001..002 Runner security: self-hosted without protection, missing timeouts flow.py GHA-FLOW-001..003 Workflow flow: workflow_run chains, composite action refs, secrets:inherit

docs.title: Config (config.py)
docs.text:
ScannerConfig holds configurable safe lists and check settings:

  • skip_checks: list of rule IDs to disable
  • min_severity: minimum severity threshold
  • trusted_action_owners: action owners considered safe (e.g., actions, github)
  • known_oidc_actions: actions that legitimately consume OIDC tokens
  • github_hosted_patterns: runner label patterns for GitHub-hosted runners
  • secret_patterns: string prefixes that indicate hardcoded credentials

Configuration is loaded from a YAML file via --config.

docs.title: Formatter (formatter.py)
docs.text:
Three output formats:

  • JSON: full findings with summary by severity and category
  • SARIF 2.1.0: standard static analysis format for GitHub Code Scanning integration
  • Text: human-readable with per-finding details and severity summary

docs.title: CLI (cli.py)
docs.text:
Entry point that wires everything together:

  1. Parse arguments
  2. Load config
  3. Parse target (file or directory)
  4. Run checks
  5. Apply baseline (if provided)
  6. Format and output
  7. Determine exit code based on findings and threshold

docs.title: Design Decisions
docs.text:
Why per-file checks + correlation checks? Most security issues are within a single workflow, but some (like workflow_run chains) require cross-file analysis. The two-tier registry keeps single-file checks simple while enabling cross-workflow correlation.

Why model composite actions as workflows? Using a unified GHAWorkflow type for both workflows and composite actions means check functions work on both without special cases. The composite_action pseudo-trigger distinguishes them when needed.

Why ruamel.yaml round-trip mode? Preserving line numbers is critical for accurate finding locations. ruamel.yaml's lc (line/column) attributes on parsed nodes provide this.

    mkdocs.yml           # Documentation config
    docs/                # Documentation source

docs.title: Adding a New Check
docs.text:
See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full guide.

Quick summary:

  1. Add your check function in the appropriate module under github_guard/checks/
  2. Use the @register_check decorator (or @register_correlation_check for cross-workflow checks)
  3. Add positive and negative tests
  4. Update _EXPECTED_MIN_CHECKS in github_guard/checks/__init__.py
  5. Document the rule in site/docs/reference/rules.md

docs.title: Binary Download
docs.text:
Pre-built binaries are available on the Releases page for:

  • Linux (amd64)
  • macOS (arm64)
  • Windows (amd64)

Download and make executable:

curl -L https://github.com/ugiordan/github-guard/releases/latest/download/github-guard-linux-amd64 -o github-guard
chmod +x github-guard
./github-guard --help

docs.title: Pre-commit Hook
docs.text:
Add to your .pre-commit-config.yaml:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/ugiordan/github-guard
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: github-guard

This runs automatically on any changes to .github/workflows/ YAML files.

docs.text:
Point github-guard at a repository root. It automatically finds .github/workflows/*.yml and action.yml files:

github-guard /path/to/repo

docs.text: github-guard .github/workflows/ci.yml

docs.title: Text (human-readable)
docs.text:
github-guard . --format text

GitHub Actions Security Scan: my-project
Found 3 issue(s)

[CRITICAL] GHA-TRIG-001: pull_request_target with fork checkout
  File: .github/workflows/ci.yml:15
  Job 'build' checks out fork code (ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }})
  in a pull_request_target workflow. This allows arbitrary code execution with
  write permissions and secrets access.
  Fix: Use pull_request trigger instead, or avoid checking out fork code.

[HIGH] GHA-PERM-001: Missing permissions block
  File: .github/workflows/ci.yml:1
  Workflow has no top-level permissions and not all jobs define permissions.
  Fix: Add a top-level 'permissions: {}' to restrict to read-only by default.

[MEDIUM] GHA-PIN-001: Unpinned action reference
  File: .github/workflows/ci.yml:10
  Action 'actions/checkout@v4' in job 'build' uses mutable ref 'v4'.
  Fix: Pin 'actions/checkout' to a specific commit SHA instead of 'v4'.

docs.text:
Only report HIGH and CRITICAL findings:

github-guard . --min-severity HIGH --format text

docs.title: CI Gate
docs.text:
Exit 1 only for HIGH+ findings (ignore MEDIUM and below):

github-guard . --fail-on HIGH

Always exit 0 (informational run):

github-guard . --exit-zero

docs.title: Baseline Management
docs.text:
Save current findings as accepted:

github-guard . --update-baseline .github-guard-baseline.json

Suppress known findings in future runs:

github-guard . --baseline .github-guard-baseline.json

docs.title: Basic scan
docs.text:
name: Security Scan
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  github-guard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install git+https://github.com/ugiordan/github-guard.git
      - run: github-guard . --format text --fail-on HIGH

docs.title: With SARIF upload
docs.text:
Upload results to GitHub Code Scanning for inline PR annotations:

name: Security Scan
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write

jobs:
  github-guard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install git+https://github.com/ugiordan/github-guard.git
      - run: github-guard . --format sarif --output results.sarif --exit-zero
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        with:
          sarif_file: results.sarif

docs.text:

- run: github-guard . --baseline .github-guard-baseline.json --format text --fail-on HIGH

  image: python:3.12-slim

docs.title: JSON output for downstream processing
docs.text:
- run: github-guard . --format json --output results.json --exit-zero
- name: Process results
  run: |
    total=$(jq '.summary.total' results.json)
    echo "Found $total findings"
    if [ "$total" -gt 0 ]; then
      jq '.findings[] | "\(.severity) \(.rule_id): \(.title)"' results.json
    fi

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: github-guard can be configured via a YAML file passed with --config.

docs.title: Config File Format
docs.text:
Create a .github-guard.yaml in your repository root:

# Skip specific checks
skip_checks:
  - GHA-PIN-001    # We accept mutable action tags in this repo
  - GHA-RUN-002    # Timeout not required for our workflows

# Minimum severity to report (default: LOW)
min_severity: MEDIUM

# Action owners considered safe (extends default list)
trusted_action_owners:
  - actions
  - github
  - azure
  - aws-actions
  - google-github-actions
  - docker
  - pypa
  - my-org          # Your organization

# Actions that legitimately consume OIDC tokens
known_oidc_actions:
  - aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials
  - google-github-actions/auth
  - Azure/login
  - pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish

# Runner label patterns for GitHub-hosted runners
# (used to distinguish self-hosted runners)
github_hosted_patterns:
  - ubuntu-*
  - windows-*
  - macos-*
  - my-custom-hosted-*   # Custom GitHub-hosted runner labels

# String prefixes that indicate hardcoded credentials
secret_patterns:
  - ghp_
  - gho_
  - ghu_
  - ghs_
  - ghr_
  - AKIA
  - sk-
  - sk_live_
  - sk_test_
  - xoxb-
  - xoxp-
  - xapp-
  - SG.
  - key-

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: github-guard . --config .github-guard.yaml

docs.title: Default Values
docs.text:
When no config file is provided, github-guard uses sensible defaults:

Setting Default skip_checks [] (all checks enabled) min_severity LOW trusted_action_owners actions, github, azure, aws-actions, google-github-actions, docker, pypa known_oidc_actions aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials, google-github-actions/auth, Azure/login, pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish github_hosted_patterns ubuntu-*, windows-*, macos-* secret_patterns ghp_, gho_, ghu_, ghs_, ghr_, AKIA, sk-, sk_live_, sk_test_, xoxb-, xoxp-, xapp-, SG., key-

docs.title: Overriding via CLI
docs.text:
The --min-severity CLI flag overrides the config file value:

# Config says min_severity: LOW, but this run only shows HIGH+
github-guard . --config .github-guard.yaml --min-severity HIGH

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
github-guard [OPTIONS] TARGET

TARGET is a path to a repository directory (scans .github/workflows/ and action.yml files) or a single YAML file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Description Default TARGET Path to a repo directory or a single YAML file (required) --format, -f Output format: json, sarif, text json --output, -o Write output to file instead of stdout stdout --config, -c Path to config file (.github-guard.yaml) None --min-severity Minimum severity to report: INFO, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL LOW (from config) --fail-on Exit 1 only if findings at or above this severity any finding --exit-zero Always exit 0 regardless of findings false --baseline Baseline file to suppress known findings None --update-baseline Write current findings as a new baseline file None --explain RULE_ID Show detailed information about a specific check rule None

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 No findings (or --exit-zero / --fail-on threshold not met) 1 Findings detected (at or above --fail-on threshold) 2 Error (invalid target, unknown rule for --explain)

  "version": "1.0.0",
  "scanner": "github-guard",
  "scan_date": "2026-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "target": ".",
  "findings": [
    {
      "rule_id": "GHA-TRIG-001",
      "severity": "CRITICAL",
      "title": "pull_request_target with fork checkout",
      "file": ".github/workflows/ci.yml",
      "line_start": 15,
      "line_end": 15,

docs.title: Finding fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description rule_id string Unique check identifier (e.g., GHA-TRIG-001) severity string CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or INFO title string Short human-readable title file string Path to the workflow file line_start int Line number where the issue was found line_end int End line number message string Detailed explanation of the issue cwe string CWE identifier (e.g., CWE-94) remediation string How to fix the issue docs_url string Link to the rule documentation

Additional context fields (e.g., job, ref, action, input) are included when relevant.

docs.title: Detection Rules
docs.text: github-guard runs 16 security checks across 6 categories. Each check has a unique ID, severity level, CWE mapping, and actionable remediation.

docs.title: GHA-TRIG-001: pull_request_target with fork checkout
docs.text:
Property Value Severity CRITICAL CWE CWE-94 (Code Injection) Category triggers

Detection logic: Flags workflows triggered by pull_request_target that use actions/checkout with a ref: pointing to fork code (github.event.pull_request.head, github.head_ref, or refs/pull/).

Why it matters: pull_request_target runs with the base repository's permissions and secrets. Checking out fork code in this context allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code with write access to the target repository.

Remediation: Use pull_request trigger instead. If pull_request_target is required, do not check out fork code, or run the checkout in a separate job with permissions: {} and no secrets.

Vulnerable 
on: pull_request_target
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - run: npm test  # Executes attacker's code with write permissions
Safe 
on: pull_request
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm test

docs.title: GHA-TRIG-002: Bypassable fork detection via repo name comparison
docs.text:
Property Value Severity HIGH CWE CWE-290 (Authentication Bypass by Spoofing) Category triggers

Detection logic: Flags if: conditions that compare github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository as a security gate, but only when the job or step also uses secrets or GITHUB_TOKEN.

Why it matters: An attacker can rename their fork to match the target repository name, bypassing this check entirely.

Remediation: Use github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork == true instead, or move sensitive operations to a workflow_run pattern.

Vulnerable 
on: pull_request_target
jobs:
  deploy:
    if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: deploy.sh
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
Safe 
on: pull_request_target
jobs:
  deploy:
    if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork != true
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: deploy.sh
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}

docs.title: GHA-TRIG-003: Unvalidated workflow_dispatch input in shell command
docs.text:
Property Value Severity MEDIUM CWE CWE-78 (OS Command Injection) Category triggers

Detection logic: Finds workflow_dispatch inputs of type string (or untyped, which defaults to string) that are interpolated directly into run: blocks via ${{ github.event.inputs.* }} or ${{ inputs.* }}.

Why it matters: Anyone with write access can trigger the workflow with crafted input values, injecting arbitrary shell commands.

Remediation: Use environment variables instead of direct interpolation, or use type: choice to restrict allowed values.

Vulnerable 
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        type: string
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo ${{ github.event.inputs.version }}
Safe 
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        type: string
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "$VERSION"
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}

docs.title: GHA-PERM-001: Missing permissions block
docs.text:
Property Value Severity HIGH CWE CWE-250 (Execution with Unnecessary Privileges) Category permissions

Detection logic: Flags workflows that have no top-level permissions: and where not all jobs define their own permissions:. Skips workflow_call-only workflows (they inherit caller permissions).

Why it matters: Without explicit permissions, the GITHUB_TOKEN gets broad default access including write to contents, packages, and pull-requests.

Remediation: Add a top-level permissions: {} to restrict to read-only by default, then grant specific permissions per job as needed.

Vulnerable 
on: push
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # GITHUB_TOKEN has write access to everything
Safe 
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

docs.title: GHA-PERM-002: id-token:write without OIDC consumer
docs.text:
Property Value Severity MEDIUM CWE CWE-250 (Execution with Unnecessary Privileges) Category permissions

Detection logic: Flags id-token: write in permissions (top-level or per-job) when no job uses a known OIDC consumer action (e.g., aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials, google-github-actions/auth).

Why it matters: Granting id-token:write allows OIDC token minting. If no action consumes the token, it is either unnecessary or could be misused to impersonate the workflow.

Remediation: Remove id-token: write if not needed, or ensure it is consumed by a known OIDC action.

docs.title: GHA-PIN-001: Unpinned action reference
docs.text:
Property Value Severity MEDIUM CWE CWE-829 (Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere) Category pinning

Detection logic: Flags action uses: references that are not pinned to a full commit SHA (40 or 64 hex characters). Skips local (./) and docker:// references.

Why it matters: Mutable tags like v4 or main can be overwritten by the action maintainer (or an attacker who compromises their account), silently replacing the action code.

Remediation: Pin to a specific commit SHA: actions/checkout@a5ac7e51b41094c92402da3b24376905380afc29.

Vulnerable 
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
Safe 
- uses: actions/checkout@a5ac7e51b41094c92402da3b24376905380afc29 # v4

docs.title: GHA-PIN-002: Unpinned container image
docs.text:
Property Value Severity MEDIUM CWE CWE-829 (Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere) Category pinning

Detection logic: Flags container images in container: or services: that use :latest tag, or have no tag at all (defaults to :latest). Images with @sha256: digest are always accepted. Skips ${{ }} expressions (dynamic images).

Why it matters: Container images using :latest or no tag can change without notice, introducing supply chain risk.

Remediation: Pin to a specific version tag or @sha256: digest.

docs.title: GHA-SEC-001: Hardcoded credential in workflow
docs.text:
Property Value Severity HIGH CWE CWE-798 (Use of Hard-coded Credentials) Category secrets

Detection logic: Scans env: values and run: blocks for known secret prefixes (ghp_, AKIA, sk-, xoxb-, etc.). Skips ${{ secrets.* }} references, URLs, version strings, git SHAs, and other common false positive patterns.

Why it matters: Hardcoded credentials in workflow files are visible to anyone with read access to the repository and cannot be rotated without a code change.

Remediation: Move the credential to GitHub Secrets and reference it as ${{ secrets.SECRET_NAME }}.

docs.title: GHA-SEC-002: Secret passed as workflow input
docs.text:
Property Value Severity MEDIUM CWE CWE-532 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File) Category secrets

Detection logic: Flags reusable workflow calls that pass secrets via with: instead of the secrets: key.

Why it matters: Secrets passed as inputs may appear in workflow logs, since GitHub only masks values passed through the secrets: mechanism.

Remediation: Move the secret from with: to secrets: in the reusable workflow call.

docs.title: GHA-SEC-003: Artifact upload in PR target context
docs.text:
Property Value Severity HIGH CWE CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information) Category secrets

Detection logic: Flags actions/upload-artifact in pull_request_target workflows. Skips jobs with empty permissions (permissions: {}), and steps with fork-detection if: conditions.

Why it matters: Artifacts uploaded with base repo privileges in a pull_request_target workflow may contain sensitive build outputs or secrets from the runner, accessible to anyone with repo read access.

Remediation: Restrict artifact uploads with an if: condition checking github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork != true, or set restrictive job permissions.

docs.title: GHA-RUN-001: Self-hosted runner without environment protection
docs.text:
Property Value Severity HIGH CWE CWE-284 (Improper Access Control) Category runners

Detection logic: Flags jobs running on self-hosted runners (not matching GitHub-hosted patterns) in externally-triggerable workflows (pull_request, issue_comment, etc.) without an environment: protection gate. Skips trusted-only triggers (push, schedule, workflow_dispatch).

Why it matters: Without environment protection, any external contributor can submit a PR that executes arbitrary code on your self-hosted infrastructure.

Remediation: Add an environment: gate that requires approval, or switch to GitHub-hosted runners for untrusted workloads.

docs.title: GHA-RUN-002: Job without timeout
docs.text:
Property Value Severity LOW CWE CWE-400 (Uncontrolled Resource Consumption) Category runners

Detection logic: Flags jobs without timeout-minutes in workflows with external triggers (excluding trusted-only and pull_request-only workflows). Skips reusable workflow calls with no steps.

Why it matters: Without a timeout, jobs can run up to the platform maximum (6 hours for GitHub-hosted, 5 days for self-hosted), wasting compute resources or enabling crypto mining abuse.

Remediation: Add timeout-minutes: 30 (or an appropriate value) to the job.

docs.title: GHA-FLOW-001: workflow_run triggered by fork-triggerable workflow
docs.text:
Property Value Severity MEDIUM CWE CWE-94 (Code Injection) Category flow

Detection logic: Cross-workflow correlation check. Identifies workflows triggered by workflow_run where the referenced trigger workflow is fork-triggerable (pull_request or pull_request_target). Only flags when the referenced workflow name matches an actual workflow in the scan.

Why it matters: A workflow_run workflow inherits some context from the triggering workflow. If the trigger is fork-triggerable, an attacker can craft PR metadata to influence the downstream workflow's behavior.

Remediation: Validate all data from github.event.workflow_run before use. Do not check out code from the triggering PR without sanitization.

docs.title: GHA-FLOW-002: Composite action with unpinned refs
docs.text:
Property Value Severity MEDIUM CWE CWE-829 (Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere) Category flow

Detection logic: Flags action references in composite actions (action.yml) that are not pinned to a commit SHA. Skips local (./) and docker:// references.

Why it matters: Composite actions inherit the same supply chain risks as workflows. Unpinned refs in composite actions can be silently replaced with malicious code.

Remediation: Pin all action references in composite actions to full commit SHAs.

docs.title: GHA-FLOW-003: Reusable workflow with secrets:inherit
docs.text:
Property Value Severity MEDIUM CWE CWE-250 (Execution with Unnecessary Privileges) Category flow

Detection logic: Flags reusable workflow calls that use secrets: inherit for external workflow refs (not ./ local). Local workflows are not flagged since they are under the same repository's control.

Why it matters: secrets: inherit passes ALL repository secrets to the called workflow. If the called workflow is compromised, all secrets are exposed.

Remediation: Explicitly pass only the secrets needed: secrets: { MY_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MY_SECRET }} } instead of secrets: inherit.

Vulnerable 
jobs:
  build:
    uses: other-org/workflows/.github/workflows/build.yml@main
    secrets: inherit  # Passes ALL secrets
Safe 
jobs:
  build:
    uses: other-org/workflows/.github/workflows/build.yml@main
    secrets:
      DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
